title: Introduce eval orchestration state machine with granular retry policies
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: intermittent CI failures from eval runs are masking real regressions and slowing down ship velocity. This change introduces a small, deterministic state machine that orchestrates multi-stage eval jobs (prepare -> run -> analyze -> finalize) and attaches configurable, per-stage retry backoff policies so we only retry transient failures (infrastructure/timeouts) while surface-level metric regressions fail fast. The goal is to reduce noisy flakes, provide clearer CI signals, and allow downstream gates to make decisions based on stable aggregated metrics. What changed: added an orchestration state machine implementation, a retry policy DSL, integration with the existing CI reporter, new metrics/labels for per-stage durations and retry counts, and unit/integration tests. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-5421) - [x] state machine core implemented - [x] retry policy DSL and default profiles added - [x] CI integration + reporter changes - [x] unit tests and integration smoke - [x] docs and upgrade notes updated Usage notes: default behavior preserves previous semantics for simple eval jobs; customers opt into the stateful orchestration via ci/pipeline config flag 'orchestrator:v1'. Operators can tune retry profiles at the job level and use the new metric 'eval_orchestrator_retry_count' to alert on noisy workloads. See docs/eval-orchestration.md for quickstart and examples.

review_comments: Connor Blake: The state transitions look clean. One request: can we add a short-circuit to skip the analyze stage if upstream provides a cached artifact? Currently analyze always runs, which duplicates work.
Priya Patel: Good catch — added a cache-checking transition and a unit test to cover cached artifact short-circuiting (see commit 3).
Jules Kim: CI integration looks good, but the timeout defaults seem long for unit CI. Can we make the pipeline defaults tighter and rely on stage-level overrides for long-running workloads?
Priya Patel: Updated defaults to 30s/2m/5m for prepare/run/analyze in the pipeline template; documentation notes how to override per-job.
Marcos Li: minor nit: please add a metric tag for 'job_family' to differentiate frequent small evals vs heavy integration evals.
Priya Patel: Added job_family tag to metrics and test assertions.

ci_notes: Flaky tests flagged by the flake-detector were quarantined in this branch; quarantines are tracked in Linear ENG-5487. Integration smoke was rerun twice due to transient infra timeouts before stabilizing.
release_notes: - Introduced eval orchestration state machine with configurable per-stage retry/backoff profiles; opt-in via ci/pipeline config 'orchestrator:v1'.; - Added metrics: eval_orchestrator_stage_duration_seconds, eval_orchestrator_retry_count, labels: job_family.; - CI now emits clearer pass/fail signals by distinguishing infra flakes from metric regressions.
upgrade_instructions: To enable orchestrator for a pipeline add 'orchestrator: v1' to your eval-ci.yaml and optionally specify retry profiles. No model or prompt changes required. Monitor eval_orchestrator_retry_count for noisy workloads and tune job_family-specific profiles.
tests_summary: Added 12 new unit tests covering transitions and retry logic; added one integration smoke test that exercises an end-to-end eval job with a simulated transient failure to validate retry behavior.
performance_impact: Small CPU overhead in coordinator process (~3-4% latency increase on short jobs) but significantly reduced re-run rates observed in canary (estimated 30% fewer flaky reruns in internal canary over 2 weeks).
notes_for_qa: QA should validate: 1) short-circuit cache path on cached artifacts, 2) retry backoffs and jitter behavior, 3) metric tagging (job_family) surfaces correctly in dashboards, 4) opt-in pipeline flag does not affect non-orchestrated jobs.
